findings.reason: it moves the recognition hook from the in-process guard to whatever runs after the payload dies, changing the section's placement and its done-when.
findings.text: §3 asserts the lane guard "reads its compilation cache … it is the right place to recognise this", but scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_guard.py is loaded only as a pytest plugin (`-p cache_guard`, run.sh:26) and reports at pytest_sessionfinish, which a SIGABRT (exit 134) never reaches, so the named owner cannot observe the abort it is meant to name

findings.reason: naming the owner redirects §3 to extend the launcher's terminal record rather than fork a parallel classifier in the cache guard.
findings.text: the plan adds a second abort-recognition surface rather than extending the owner that already writes the run's terminal line (EXIT_STATUS=…/NOVA_LANE_EXIT_STATUS=…) and its header (run.sh:135-150) from outside the payload, which is the only thing that survives the abort

findings.reason: the child-surviving, fixed-interval sampler is genuinely a different measurement from the self-sampling pytest plugin, so the omission is a prior-art account gap rather than a design change.
findings.text: the plan proposes the §1 /proc mapping sampler without citing the existing mapping recollection (totals["all"]["mapping_count"] from /proc/self/smaps) or the compile-memory measurement in benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py, so the reuse map for the sampler is incomplete

findings.reason: the sections must account for the added interface surface in their own text before the first implementation node is released.
findings.text: with the supplied counts all zero, §1 introduces the compile_abort_probe CLI and §3 introduces an abort-classifier/refusal family, and neither section states what it retires or merges or why nothing can

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py hides child-process /proc sampling, liveness handling and summary emission behind sample_child plus main, a small interface over substantial behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the terminal run record the §3 log line parallels is already owned by scripts/nova_lane/run.sh:185 (EXIT_STATUS=/NOVA_LANE_EXIT_STATUS), which prints the lane header and survives the process; the plan adds a parallel recognition surface in cache_guard instead of extending that owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 adds a probe CLI (--samples/--summary/--interval) and §3 adds a classification/refusal family, and no section names what it retires or merges or states why nothing can.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the lane's cache guard and the persistent compilation cache as prior art for §3 and §2, but never searches the mapping/memory-measurement space it extends in §1, so it does not cite benchmarks/lane_resource_accumulation.py (records process mapping_count via /proc/self/smaps) or benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 places the compile-abort classifier in the in-process cache_guard pytest plugin, a thin extension of a cache-accounting guard that is killed by the very abort it must classify, with no statement of why the launcher's own terminal record cannot carry it.
